title: A Member could use another user's private gateway.
proof: The Member could not list or read the private gateway. Supplying its raw ID during agent launch still produced a working opaque capability, and the control plane injected the owner's canary credential.
limit: The attacker needs the high-entropy gateway ID. Cross-organization use and universal ID discovery were not demonstrated.
fix: Enforce owner and organization authorization again when every attachment ID is resolved.

title: A sandboxed agent could steer a server-side gateway.
proof: An owned callback proved the request came from Runloop's gateway service, not the Devbox. A link-local target returned a live HTTP response.
limit: IMDSv2 blocked credential retrieval. No metadata token, IAM role, cloud credential, or cross-tenant data was obtained.
fix: Resolve and reject private destinations before connecting, then repeat validation after every redirect and DNS answer.

title: OAuth setup followed a public redirect into loopback.
proof: Before any MCP config or agent existed, the Reflex host fetched attacker-selected OAuth metadata. An owned 307 preserved its registration POST and redirected it into loopback without destination revalidation.
limit: The tested path exposed no internal response body, cloud token, administrative action, or cross-tenant data. Distinct failures provided only a behavior oracle.
fix: Allow public HTTPS OAuth endpoints only and re-resolve and revalidate discovery, registration, token, and redirect destinations.

title: The MCP test returned part of the server's response.
proof: A unique marker returned by an owned HTTP 500 endpoint appeared inside the authenticated connection-test error. A controlled redirect also converted POST to GET.
limit: Only selected error bodies were reflected. No sensitive internal service, cloud credential, control-plane authority, or cross-organization data was reached.
fix: Allow public HTTPS only, disable or revalidate redirects, and never reflect upstream bodies verbatim.

title: The file boundary stopped files. The shell walked around it.
proof: The guarded file tool rejected an outside-root marker. The command tool read the same marker from the real connected Mac.
limit: This requires a user to connect their own workstation with read-write access. It is not Runloop infrastructure compromise.
fix: Apply the selected-root policy to commands, subprocesses, redirections, paths, and inherited environment.
